title: ASEAN Statement Calls on Nations to Safeguard Journalism Against Artificial Intelligence
key_facts: Media and intellectual property leaders from Southeast Asian nations met in Bali on 10 Oct 2026 and adopted the ASEAN Joint Declaration.
Four commitments: recognise journalism's economic value, strengthen copyright frameworks, trade justice for platforms, regional cooperation.
It targets content aggregation, scraping and AI data mining without compensation.
Member countries will develop national regulatory roadmaps including cross-border takedown, collective licensing, AI compensation frameworks and digital watermarking.
Speakers included Indonesian Press Council chairman Komaruddin Hidayat and Indonesian law ministry director general Hermansyah Siregar.
Thailand is negotiating with Google on media worker training and revenue sharing.
quote_evidence: Media and intellectual property leaders from Southeast Asian nations convened in Bali on October 10, 2026, to adopt the ASEAN Joint Declaration, addressing threats to journalism from digital platforms and artificial intelligence.
Member countries will develop national regulatory roadmaps, including cross-border takedown mechanisms, collective licensing schemes, AI compensation frameworks, and digital watermarking
why_it_matters_hint: Regional push to make AI and platform companies pay for news content.
notes: The article ends with the line “Source : ASEAN Declaration Urges States to Protect Press from AI”, i.e. it rests on an earlier article. The article gives no dates or enforcement details. Pool score 5 lowered to 4: event five days old, rewritten report.
